properties.description:
Six cases, of which the MERGE is the one carrying the weight. A replacing setter here would be this codebase's most-repeated defect — a write path that builds a node from a partial property set and erases what the caller did not name, fixed four times already — arriving in the one place where the value erased is a person's own vocabulary. Proven by negative control: replacing the merge with an assignment fails exactly the two merge cases and leaves the other four green, so the tests pin the merge specifically rather than the feature generally.

The others pin the boundaries that are judgements rather than mechanics: recording an alias RENAMES NOTHING (name, description and status must be byte-identical after), passing no terms is REFUSED with a message saying that omission is not how you clear them, and a type that names a STATEMENT rather than a thing is refused with all five accepted types named in the refusal.
properties.name: a_node_records_what_the_user_calls_it.rs — the user's own word reaches the node, a second word never costs the first, and passing none is refused rather than treated as a clear
